audio_caption: The audio begins with soft, contemplative music that sets a relaxed mood. A female speaker then shares her surprise that some people haven't heard of using baking soda in hair care, stating, "I was a little shocked...that a lot of you have never heard of people putting baking soda in their hair." She describes it as "a thing, like a popular thing," expressing how easy it is to encounter information online about baking soda's supposed benefits, encouraging listeners to try it out on their own hair. The music fades out as the speaker concludes her thought.

A single female speaker with an informative tone begins discussing the use of baking soda on hair, noting how information can change. She recommends looking out for her people and providing information. She offers that if one plans on trying it, they should have a better understanding. Then, she announces that links to two videos regarding baking soda for hair will be in the description. Shifting gears, she mentions taking a close look at how baking soda and apple cider vinegar interact. The audio ends with her inviting listeners to sit back, relax, and enjoy the video. The audio is relatively clean, with very few background sounds.

The audio begins with a calm, clear female voice discussing the properties of apple cider vinegar and baking soda, describing apple cider vinegar as "a good bacterium filled acid" and baking soda as "an alkaline salt called sodium bicarbonate." She mentions the use of baking soda and apple cider vinegar in hair care, transitioning into an intention to discuss the methods. Before proceeding, she states "there's something I want to clear up," ending the initial segment. The audio concludes with a quick ascending musical flourish.

The clip concludes with a male saying "hi".

The clip begins with background music that is moody. A female speaker begins advising against excessive use of baking soda on hair, suggesting to dilute it and use a diluted ACV rinse to prevent obstruction of skin cells around hair follicles. Then the sound of a ding can be heard.

The audio clip begins with a single female speaker discussing a baking soda and apple cider vinegar treatment for hair and scalp, emphasizing its potential for deep cleaning follicles. This is followed by the sound of a soft "shh".

She concludes by stating that there's a "chemical reaction" to understand, suggesting a technical explanation is to follow.

The audio clip features a single, calm and informational female speaker explaining the chemical reaction that occurs when mixing baking soda and apple cider vinegar, noting that carbonic acid decomposes until equilibrium. She describes the release of carbon dioxide as a gas, causing bubbling and fizzing. This speech is accompanied by the continuous sound of quiet, gentle music, with an uplifting and calm mood.

The audio clip begins with a female speaker explaining that after carbon dioxide escapes, you're left with sodium acetate, which is salt and water, and that the solution is somewhere in the neutral area. She then says, "saltwater is actually really good for your scalp from time to time," especially if you have scalp issues. She notes that it detoxifies elements, reduces inflammation, heals cuts, provides some surfactant action, and removes oily product buildup.

The audio clip features one female speaker warning about the dangers of sodium acetate for hair, particularly its drying effect, advising against frequent use and suggesting it as an occasional scalp treatment. She also mentions that saltwater of any kind can make hair feel stiff. The speaker maintains an informative and cautious tone throughout the clip.

The audio begins with a female speaker outlining a hair care routine, including instructions to "reinforce your cuticles." She presents an alternative method involving "sea salt with two cups of warm water", describing a pH level of "five and six". She continues with advice about proper hair care sequences, concluding the section with "I hope it was helpful."  She then invites viewers to ask questions and mentions being on Instagram.
